title: Climbing Stairs
summary: Count the different ways to climb n steps when each move climbs one or two steps.

tests.explain: Two single steps, or one double step.
1 + 1 + 1, 1 + 2 and 2 + 1. Order matters, so 1 + 2 and 2 + 1 are different climbs.
The last move lands on step 5 from step 4 (5 ways to get there) or from step 3 (3 ways): 5 + 3 = 8.

hints: Look at the very last move onto step n. Where could you have been standing just before it?
ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2). Plain recursion on that is exponential and times out at n = 45: memoize it, or fill an array from the bottom up.
Each value needs only the two before it. Start from ways(0) = 1 and ways(1) = 1 and roll two variables up to n.

complexity.time: O(n): one pass from step 2 to step n
complexity.space: O(1): only the last two counts are kept
